J1_line_asserts_challenged_proposition.justification: The response challenges "The abelianization G/G' is isomorphic to the center Z(G)." First-choice line 13 is the parenthetical justification of the proof's next step: "<=> (Since G/G'~Z(G) )". Under the source's own notation (line 1: G' = [G,G], the derived subgroup) and with G an arbitrary group -- no hypothesis anywhere in the text restricts G beyond the standing G' <= N <= G of line 7 -- the line asserts exactly the isomorphism G/G' = Z(G), and the proof uses it immediately by substituting Z(G) for G/G' at line 15. So line 13 asserts the challenged proposition.

J2_evidence_specified.justification: A concrete group with both sides computed: "For G = S_3, G/G' ≅ C_2 while Z(S_3) = {e}, so they are not isomorphic" (the reasoning also names G' = A_3). The group, its derived subgroup, the quotient and the centre are all given explicitly; nothing is left to the reader.

J3_evidence_check.justification: Exact finite enumeration of the supplied witness, script kept. Building S_3 as permutations of {0,1,2}: the subgroup generated by all commutators has order 3 and equals exactly the set of even permutations (A_3), and it is normal in G, so G/G' has order 6/3 = 2 and is therefore cyclic of order 2 as the response says. The centre Z(S_3) computed by brute force is the identity alone, order 1. A group of order 2 is not isomorphic to a group of order 1, so line 13 is false at G = S_3. The witness also respects the source's standing hypothesis of line 7 (G' normal in N normal in G): the script confirms both N = G' (order 3) and N = G (order 6) are normal in G and contain G', so an admissible N exists for this G and the counterexample is not excluded by any assumption in force.

J4_consequence_overreach.justification: The response's stated consequence is confined to the located line: "they assert that G/G' is isomorphic to Z(G). That's false. So line 0013 contains the false assertion." It explicitly does not extend this to the theorem being proved -- it says of "G'<N iff G/N is abelian" that "That's true (standard result: G/N abelian iff G' <= N)" -- and it correctly distinguishes line 15 ("which follows from false assumption, also false") as a consequence rather than the assertion itself. Correct scope, no overreach.

notes: For a second reader: the only interpretive question is whether the '~' of line 13 means 'is isomorphic to'. The proof's own use makes that reading forced -- line 15 substitutes Z(G) for G/G' in the chain of line 11 -- and the intended fact there is that G/G' is the abelianization, not the centre. I also checked the response's claim about line 11 only insofar as it does not bear on the first choice; I did not grade line 11 or 15.
